title: Seawall Rules in Broward County
question: What are the seawall requirements in Broward County?
qualifier: Broward is the one county in South Florida with a single standard behind every city, and the number most people quote is the wrong one. The standard is 5 ft NAVD88 by 2050. The 4 ft figure you will hear is an allowance until 2035 that the county says a municipality MAY grant - not a floor you are entitled to. Three cities answer it three different ways, so the number that applies to you is your city's, not the county's.
detail_rows: The standard :: 5 ft NAVD88 by 1 January 2050. That is the figure the county is driving every shoreline to. | The 2035 allowance :: Until 2035 a municipality may allow 4 ft NAVD88, but only if the barrier is designed and constructed to accommodate 5 ft NAVD88 by 1 January 2050. | It is not a right :: The county's own developer guidance says the allowance "may be granted by the municipality." It is your city's call. Budget for 5 ft and treat 4 ft as the exception you have to ask for. | Where it comes from :: Broward County Code Section 39-404, Article XXV, Resiliency Standards for Tidal Flood Protection, and Broward County Land Use Plan Policy 2.21.7. | Every city had to adopt it :: Local governments were required to adopt an implementing ordinance by 13 February 2022, so the standard reaches inside every municipality in the county. | Hollywood :: Took the allowance. Its own guidance requires 4 ft NAVD88 before 1 January 2035, then 5 ft by 2050. | Fort Lauderdale :: Set 5.0 ft NAVD88. An application before 1 January 2035 may build to 4.0 ft if the wall is designed to reach 5.0 ft by 2050. | Pompano Beach :: 5 ft NAVD88 minimum and 5 ft 10 in maximum. The only city in the county that caps the height as well as setting a floor. | The practical point :: Build to 4 ft today and the wall has to come up again before 2050. Ask what it costs to build to 5 ft now, while the barge is already there.
source: Broward County Code Sec. 39-404, Art. XXV, Resiliency Standards for Tidal Flood Protection; Broward County Land Use Plan Policy 2.21.7; Broward County "Build It High, Keep It Dry" developer guidance; City of Hollywood Sea Walls and Other Tidal Flood Barriers brochure

title: Seawall Rules in Miami-Dade County
question: What are the seawall requirements in Miami-Dade County?
unit: the number is set by your city
qualifier: Miami-Dade works the opposite way to Broward. The county runs the environmental permit through Chapter 24, but it sets no countywide seawall elevation — that is your city's decision, and the cities differ sharply. What the county does control is how far waterward you may rebuild, and that single measurement decides which permit route you are on.
detail_rows: The county's part :: Chapter 24 environmental permitting through DERM, which applies inside every city in the county. | The 18-inch rule :: A seawall rebuilt at the mean high water line or up to 18 inches waterward of its existing line (or up to 18 inches beyond existing support piles that stick out no more than 14 inches) qualifies for a short-form permit decided by DERM. Seawall-only work cannot be pulled into a County Commission hearing. Since Ord. 25-73 (July 2025), standard-form applications are also decided by the DERM Director, except for variances that require a hearing or substantial changes to a Commission-approved permit or covenant. | Why that matters :: Beyond 18 inches, the county's delegated state and federal authority may not apply, so separate state (FDEP) and Army Corps approval may be needed (Ord. 25-73 recitals). For short-form seawall permits the county targets a completeness review within 10 days and a decision within 90 days after it (Ord. 25-73 Sec. 8, from 1 Dec 2025). | Where it is written :: Miami-Dade County Code Section 24-48.2, as amended by Ord. 25-73 (7-1-25). | Elevation is municipal :: The county sets no height. Miami Beach requires 5.7 ft NAVD88. Other cities set their own, and several have not published one at all. | Miami Beach specifically :: 5.7 ft NAVD88 for new or substantially improved walls, with an interim 4.0 ft allowed for lesser repairs if the wall is built to accept 5.7 ft later. Substantial now means repairs of $500 or more per linear foot, raised from $300 in July 2025. | Budget for a bond :: Some cities in the county require a refundable bond on top of the contract. Confirm the current amount with the city - it is not in the contractor's bid. Ask before you sign.
source: Miami-Dade County Code Sec. 24-48.2 (as amended by Ord. 25-73, 7-1-25); City of Miami Beach Code Sec. 54-62(a), Ordinance 2025-4754

title: Seawall Rules in Palm Beach County
question: What are the seawall requirements in Palm Beach County?
qualifier: Palm Beach is the hardest of the four counties to get a straight answer in. Broward has one standard every city adopted; Palm Beach does not work that way. Each town we have verified sets its own elevation, in its own document, and two neighbouring towns can differ. Worse, the rule is often not in the code where you would look for it.
detail_rows: How this county differs :: Broward's towns all adopted one county standard. The Palm Beach towns we have verified each set their own, independently, and cite no county mandate. | Boca Raton :: 4.0 ft NAVD88 minimum, 6.0 ft maximum. The wall must also be built so a further 12 to 18 inches can be added later without altering it. | Where Boca hides it :: Not in the ordinance. Chapter 22 covers marine structures, but the elevation lives in the Engineering Design Standards Manual, section 7.7. Searching the code finds nothing. | Delray Beach :: 4.2 ft NAVD88 minimum on every waterfront property. The maximum varies with your FEMA flood zone — your base flood elevation where that is 5.0 ft or higher, 5 ft where the BFE is 4.0. | Delray's extra obligation :: Any contract to sell property in a tidally influenced area of Delray Beach, signed after 1 February 2022, must carry a tidal flood barrier disclosure in bold capitals of at least 14 point. That is a standing duty on every waterfront listing in the city. | Build low, engineer high :: Both towns require a wall built under the higher figure to be designed so it can be raised later. Building to the minimum today does not close the question. | What to ask your town :: What is the minimum cap elevation, in which datum, and where is it written — the code, or an engineering standards manual? The second half of that question is the one that saves you a week.
source: City of Boca Raton Engineering Design Standards Manual § 7.7 and Code of Ordinances Ch. 22; City of Delray Beach Land Development Regulations Sec. 7.1.7 and Table 7.1.7(D), Ordinance 23-21

title: Seawall Rules in Monroe County and the Florida Keys
question: What are the seawall requirements in Monroe County?
qualifier: Monroe is the only county of the four where we can say with certainty that no elevation standard exists, because we read every mention of seawall and bulkhead in the county's code to establish it. That does not make the Keys permissive. Monroe regulates something the other three counties largely do not - whether you may build a vertical wall at all.
detail_rows: No minimum, no maximum :: Monroe County Land Development Code Sec. 118-12(k) sets no elevation and no datum for a seawall or bulkhead. Every seawall and bulkhead reference in the Code of Ordinances, the Land Development Code and the Comprehensive Plan was checked. | The real restriction is location :: A vertical seawall or bulkhead is permitted only to stabilise a severely eroding shoreline, and only on manmade canals, channels or basins. Sec. 118-12(k)(3). | It is a last resort :: Permitted only if native vegetation, or riprap and filter cloth, is not a feasible means to control erosion. Sec. 118-12(k)(3). | Open water is closed :: No new seawalls, bulkheads or other hardened vertical structures are permitted on open water. Comprehensive Plan Policy 210.1.6 goes further - seawalls are prohibited on any beach or open-water shoreline. | Repair is protected :: A lawfully existing deteriorated seawall may be repaired or replaced, and is exempt from the nonsubstantial-improvements limit, except on known or potential sea turtle nesting beaches. The work must keep the existing footprint to the maximum extent practicable. Sec. 118-12(k)(4). | Turtles outrank the wall :: No seawall, bulkhead or riprap on or waterward of a beach berm complex that is known or potential marine turtle nesting area, as determined by the County Biologist. Sec. 118-12(k)(7). | Riprap and mangroves :: Riprap at the toe wherever feasible, and barriers placed landward of existing mangroves whenever feasible. Sec. 118-12(k)(5) and (6). | The one height-adjacent rule :: Existing grade landward of the bulkhead must be at least six inches lower than the top of the bulkhead. Sec. 118-12(k)(2). That fixes grade against the cap. It does not tell you how high the cap must be. | A wall with no house :: A seawall without a principal use may have a cap no more than two feet wide. Sec. 118-12(k)(1). | State and federal come first :: All such projects require state and/or federal permits before construction and before the county issues a Notice to Proceed. Sec. 118-12(k)(9). A separate county permit is required for a seawall. Code of Ordinances Sec. 6-100(b). | One city does set a height :: Key Colony Beach requires 5.5 ft above mean sea level. It is the only jurisdiction in the county with a seawall elevation standard.
source: Monroe County Land Development Code Sec. 118-12(k), Shoreline Setbacks; Monroe County Comprehensive Plan Policies 210.1.6 and 212.5.1-212.5.4; Monroe County Code of Ordinances Sec. 6-100(b)
